$comment: Stands in for GET /api/v1/admin/users/analytics. MONTH-KEYED, not period-keyed, and that is the whole shape decision: a payload that ships pre-summed 30-day and 90-day blocks can only ever answer the two windows somebody thought of, so a date-range control over it is decoration. Every range-dependent figure here is a MONTHLY row with its own numerators AND denominators, so any span of months resolves to real arithmetic client-side — see rangeTotals() in views/Users/store.ts. Rates are never stored: they are numerator/denominator pairs, because a stored percentage cannot be re-aggregated over a span without lying. It counts PEOPLE ONLY — registrations, channels and profile completion. Conversion, retention, cohorts and revenue are asked of the subscription record in Finance.
$comment_granularity: The series is monthly, so the range control snaps to whole months and says so. A day-precision picker over a monthly series would promise a resolution the data does not have.
$comment_months: Per row: registrations, and profileCompleted — the share of the base that met the profile v1 threshold that month. bySource is registrations per channel and sums exactly to the month's total. The membership series (firstTimeMembers, renewals, expiries, cancellations and the three *Eligible denominators, byPlan and activeAtEnd) left with the membership feature: what a customer bought is a Finance record and its rates are computed there, against the subscription that holds the money.
$comment_engagement: null, not zero, and not an empty object. UM-OD-10 has not defined the qualifying-activity taxonomy, so DAU, WAU, MAU and member engagement rate cannot be computed. When it lands this becomes { dau, wau, mau, memberEngagementRate, taxonomyVersion }.
